title: The Morning Brief: Arc launches today; Senate kills crypto bill
dek: Circle's Arc blockchain goes live Wednesday with 11 Wall Street validators as founding operators, while the Senate blocks the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act on ethics grounds. Two institutional stories, two different outcomes.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: Arc's mainnet launch today marks the first time major financial institutions (BlackRock, DTCC, Visa, Mastercard, ICE) operate a blockchain settlement layer, but individual validator voting weights remain undisclosed. Meanwhile, the Senate's rejection of the Clarity Act on a 49-50 vote ended months of bipartisan negotiation, with seven Democrats citing inadequate ethics provisions around Trump's $1.4 billion crypto profits.
bottom_line: Arc's public launch today shows whether 11 named Wall Street validators actually operate nodes and what voting power each holds; the May 2028 deadline for Proof-of-Stake transition is the date that validates whether Circle can hold institutional participation steady while surrendering permissioned consensus. The Senate's rejection of the Clarity Act on ethics grounds signals that bipartisan crypto regulation in the U.S. requires stronger governance safeguards than the final Republican text provided.
body: Circle's Arc mainnet launches today, September 16, with 11 named founding validators from Wall Street and payments infrastructure: BlackRock, DTCC, Visa, Mastercard, ICE, and Circle itself, plus six ecosystem partners. The network uses permissioned Proof-of-Authority consensus, a rotating validator proposes a block, and more than two-thirds of the validator set must pre-commit before finalization. Circle's documentation explicitly walls off these institutions from liability for third-party applications built on top of Arc, a structural separation that could reshape how traditional finance treats crypto infrastructure. The critical unresolved questions are the individual voting weights assigned to each validator and whether real settlement activity emerges in the first weeks of operation.

On Capitol Hill, the Senate failed yesterday to advance the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, the crypto industry's most significant legislative push. A cloture motion fell short of 60 votes with a 49-50 result: four Senate Republicans (Susan Collins, Josh Hawley, Jerry Moran, Thom Tillis) joined all Democrats to block the measure. Seven Democrats who had spent months negotiating the bill's final text voted against proceeding, citing ethics provisions they said were too weak to prevent Trump and his appointees from profiting off crypto ventures while overseeing the industry. Per the reporting, Trump and his family accumulated $1.4 billion from crypto ventures in 2025 alone. Republicans released new ethics language on September 14 that incorporated 126 substantive changes Democrats had sought, but staff-level talks ended without agreement over whether the restrictions were enforceable. The collapse of the Clarity Act leaves the U.S. without a statutory digital asset framework and ends 2026 legislative work on comprehensive crypto regulation.

Elsewhere, the tape turned mixed. Bitcoin traded at $75,767.84 on the day, up 0.23 percent in 24 hours but down 5.68 percent over the week and up 18.27 percent over 30 days, per the desk's boards. Ethereum held flat at $2,397.56 on the day, down 4.63 percent weekly and up 28.31 percent monthly. The desk's Market Pulse shows the Fear and Greed Index at 51, labeled Neutral, within a 30-day range of 41 to 74. Bitcoin's RSI14 stood at 48.8, neither overbought nor oversold, while MACD remained below the signal line, suggesting momentum may not be sustained. The desk's Whale Watch board shows $76.9 million in bitcoin moving onto exchanges over the past 24 hours, with the week ending September 16 recording $558 million net moving onto exchanges. Bitcoin ETF flows turned negative on September 15, with outflows of $450.4 million on the day and net outflows of $706.6 million over the prior five sessions, a reversal from the month's earlier strength. Ethereum ETF flows disagreed: an outflow of $142.3 million on September 15 followed a net inflow of $200.0 million over five sessions. Funding rates on major altcoins remain elevated, SOL at negative 0.3 percent annualized, XRP at negative 3.3 percent, DOGE at 7.1 percent, creating asymmetric liquidation risk if sentiment shifts.

Separate from regulation and settlement, a series of security and operational incidents shaped the day. The Revolut breach exposed customer identity documents, account statements, and cryptocurrency transaction histories after an attacker impersonated a government agency to bypass information requests. Symbiosis' bridge was exploited for 46.1 billion fake syBTC tokens through two compounding software bugs, with preliminary losses estimated at 9.97 bitcoin, roughly $770,000. The DOJ charged two Robinhood engineers, Hefu Chai and Huaisong Xiang, with wire fraud and commodities fraud for trading perpetual futures on Hyperliquid using nonpublic information about cryptocurrency listings between 2025 and 2026, each earning more than $50,000 from the scheme. And the DOJ filed a civil forfeiture complaint against $61 million in cryptocurrency allegedly moved through Binance by two China-based firms to launder Iranian oil proceeds destined for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, part of a broader operation called Operation Economic Outcast targeting Iran's financial networks.

On adoption and infrastructure, India's Securities and Exchange Board completed its first tokenized corporate bond pilot on September 10, moving 1,025 crore through atomic delivery-versus-payment using private digital tokens and the Reserve Bank's wholesale digital rupee. REC Limited issued 500 crore, L&T Limited issued 500 crore, and IIFL issued 25 crore; retail participation and secondary-market trading are deferred to a later stage. Balancer's governance forum posted a proposal to wind down the protocol and return its approximately 9 million dollar treasury to BAL token holders through staged redemptions from May 2027 to July 2028, following accelerating revenue decline and a failed April restructuring. Monthly protocol revenue stood at $30,000 in August against burn of $150,000, crossing the $60,000-per-month threshold set in April that would trigger a governance review. Zcash's community governance polls closed September 14 with 2.4 million ZEC voting 99.9 percent to cut block times from 75 to 25 seconds and 98.9 percent to preserve Bitcoin-style halvings every four years. The House Ways and Means Committee released a 114-page Digital Asset Tax Certainty Act on September 14 with formal markup set for today, proposing a $10 exemption for blockchain fees that would not trigger a taxable event for users executing fewer than 5,000 transfers in a year.
